feed.title: Vidhana — Sri Lankan IRD tax and VAT gazettes — other
feed.subtitle: What changed in the Sri Lankan Inland Revenue gazettes, and what the rule is now. Derived from https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/sitepages/gazette.aspx?menuid=1602

entry.title: 1947/48 [other] new: Amend the Order published under Sec. 2(1) of the Finance Act No. 25 of 2003 with effect from 01.01.2016
entry.content:
As amended, the Order replaces Schedule I of Gazette 1791/08 and sets the charge for persons leaving Sri Lanka at US $30.00, whether they leave by aircraft or ship. The new schedule applies from 1 January 2016.
Effective from 2016-01-01.
Affects: travellers leaving Sri Lanka.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2016_1947_48_E.pdf

entry.title: 1844/62 [other] new: Writing off the Tax charged and Levied on or before 31.12.2009 on SLTB, Kesbewa and 10 other institutions on 17.12.2013
entry.content:
The Commissioner General of Inland Revenue wrote off listed tax arrears owed by 11 named institutions, including Sri Lanka Transport Board depots, government bodies and other organisations. The write-off covers tax charged and levied on or before 31 December 2009 and took effect on 17 December 2013 under the Default Taxes (Special Provisions) Act.
Effective from 2014-01-09.
Affects: taxpayers with tax already in default.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2014_1844_62_(E).pdf

entry.title: 1792/19 [other] new: The Finance Act No. 11 of 2006 - Rescission of the Gaz. Ex. No. 1709_10 of 07.06.2011
entry.content:
This order sets the permitted motor vehicle for the concession as a motor car. It sets the concessionary levy at 75% of the combined taxes payable under the Customs Ordinance, Excise (Special Provisions) Act and Value Added Tax Act, and rescinds the order published in Gazette Extraordinary No. 1709/10 of 7 June 2011.
Effective from 2013-01-09.
Affects: persons claiming the permitted motor vehicle concession.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2013_1792_19 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1760/04 [other] new: Tax Appeals Commission Act No. 23 of 2011 - The Tax Appeals Rules, 2011
entry.content:
These Rules set the procedure for appealing a Commissioner-General’s tax determination to the Tax Appeals Commission. An appellant must submit a petition with specified tax and appeal details, proof of paying 25% of the assessed amount, a non-refundable Rs. 2,500 fee, six document copies, and certified copies of supporting documents; hearing attendance and notification rules also apply.
Effective from 2012-05-28.
Affects: authorised representatives appearing before the Tax Appeals Commission; taxpayers appealing a Commissioner-General determination.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2012_1760_04 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1709/10 [other] new: The Finance Act, No. 11 of 2006 - Order under Sec. 2(1)(b)(i) and (ii)
entry.content:
This Order replaces Gazette 1680/21 and sets the permitted motor vehicle for the concession as a motor car with a cylinder capacity of no more than 1600cc. The concessionary levy is set at 75% of the total customs, excise and VAT taxes payable on the vehicle.
Effective from 2011-06-07.
Affects: persons claiming the permitted motor vehicle concession.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2011_1709_10 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1699/44 [other] new: Default Taxes (Special Provisions) 16 of 2010. Appoint the 01.04.2011 as the date on which the aforesaid Act shall come into operation
entry.content:
The Default Taxes (Special Provisions) Act, No. 16 of 2010 comes into operation on 1 April 2011. This activates the Act’s provisions for taxpayers with tax already in default.
Effective from 2011-03-31.
Affects: taxpayers with tax already in default.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2011_1699_44 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1530/17 [other] new: Debits Tax Act No. 16 of 2002. order, debits shall be exempt from debits tax
entry.content:
This order exempts specified debits from Debits Tax. The exemptions cover qualifying payments from current or savings accounts by School Development Societies for school nutrition projects, the “Api Venuwen Api” Fund, Rural Banks, and registered co-operative societies.
Effective from 2008-01-01.
Affects: banks and financial institutions collecting debits tax; holders of current and savings accounts.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20081530_17(E).pdf

entry.title: 1478/10 [other] new: Debit Tax Act No. 16 2002
entry.content:
Debits made from specified Samurdhi-related imprest accounts held at the Bank of Ceylon or People’s Bank are exempt from Debit Tax. The exemption covers accounts maintained by the Samurdhi Authority, District Secretariats, and Divisional Secretariats for transferring or using Treasury-funded imprest amounts for Samurdhi Authority activities.
Effective from 2007-01-02.
Affects: banks and financial institutions collecting debits tax; holders of current and savings accounts.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20071478_10(E).pdf

entry.title: 1478/08 [other] new: Turnover Tax Act No. 69 of 1981
entry.content:
From 1 January 2007, turnover from businesses listed in Part IX of the Schedule is taxed at 1%, while turnover from liquor and cigarettes bought from a manufacturer or importer is taxed at 5%. This adds a new 5% category specifically covering those liquor and cigarette businesses.
Effective from 2006-12-31.
Affects: businesses liable to turnover tax.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20071478_8(E).pdf
